title: A novel high-z submm galaxy efficient line survey in ALMA Bands 3 through 8 - an ANGELS pilot
question: Test the viability of a rapid snapshot-style line survey with ALMA across Bands 3 through 8 with tunings optimized to cover as many spectral lines as possible in high-redshift dusty star-forming galaxies.

what.value: Spectroscopic redshifts, unresolved velocity widths, and Band 3/4 CO and [CI] line fluxes and surface densities from BEARS

recipe.goal: Calibrate visibility data, subtract continuum, and image continuum and spectral cubes
recipe.method: Restore pipeline calibration in CASA, bin channels by 16 to locate lines, subtract continuum from visibilities using line-free channels, and image continuum and cubes with tclean using Hogbom deconvolver and 0.05 arcsec uv-taper (plus 0.5 arcsec taper for HerBS-159A/B).
key_parameters: Channel binning factor = 16 for initial line search; line exclusion window = 0.4 GHz for undetected expected lines
Natural weighting for continuum; briggsbwtaper with robust = 2 for cubes; uv-taper = 0.05 arcsec

recipe.goal: Extract spectral line profiles and measure integrated line fluxes, widths, and velocity offsets
recipe.method: Define apertures by matching Band 7 2-sigma continuum contours (and 2-sigma moment-0 contours for large sources) to the cube resolution and extending by up to 3 beams; extract spectra and fit single Gaussian profiles.
key_parameters: 2-sigma continuum and moment-0 contour thresholds, extended by up to 3 beams (no spatial smoothing for absorption lines)

recipe.goal: Model gravitational lensing and measure intrinsic source sizes and magnifications
recipe.method: Two-phase visibility-plane (uv-plane) lens modelling of Band 7 data using PyAutoLens (SIE lens + external shear; Phase 1: Sersic source, Phase 2: pixelated Voronoi mesh with constant regularization). For unlensed sources, fit Sersic profile in image plane using CASA IMFIT.
key_parameters: Sersic index n free between 0.5 and 5 for lensed sources; n = 0.5 fixed in IMFIT for unlensed sources
assumptions: Singular Isothermal Ellipsoid (SIE) lens mass profile with external shear; flat Lambda-CDM Planck 2020 cosmology (Omega_m = 0.315, Omega_Lambda = 0.685, h = 0.674)

recipe.goal: Derive infrared luminosities, dust temperatures, and dust masses
recipe.method: Fit Herschel photometry at fixed spectroscopic redshift using (1) Cosmic Eyelash template, (2) Bakx et al. (2018, 2020b) template, and (3) single-temperature modified black-body with beta_dust = 2.0; distribute multi-component luminosity by Band 7 flux ratios. For resolved luminosity, fit Band 7 flux with T_d = 35 K, beta_dust = 2 MBB.
key_parameters: T_d = 35 K, beta_dust = 2.0 for resolved Band 7 MBB; beta_dust = 2.0 for Herschel MBB fit
assumptions: Multiple components in a field have the same colour temperature and redshift; beta_dust = 2.0

recipe.goal: Construct CO SLEDs, analyze absorption line velocity offsets, and build a stacked composite spectrum
recipe.method: Combine ANGELS and BEARS CO fluxes normalized to CO(4-3) (using Harrington et al. 2021 template when CO(4-3) is absent); compare absorption line velocities to systemic CO velocities; stack spectra extracted from >2-sigma Band 7 regions (smoothed by 1 beam) normalized to z = 2.5 and L_IR = 10^13 L_sun using variance weighting.
assumptions: Harrington et al. (2021) average CO SLED template is representative for translating lowest-J CO to CO(4-3)

recipe.goal: Evaluate the resolved Schmidt-Kennicutt star-formation law and intrinsic star-formation surface densities
recipe.method: Smooth Band 7 dust continuum to the beam size of the lowest-J ANGELS CO transition; compare pixel-by-pixel (>3-sigma in one map and >1-sigma in the other) and downsample for beam independence to derive Sigma_SFR and Sigma_H2.
key_parameters: Pixel thresholds: > 3 sigma in CO or dust and > 1 sigma in the other
assumptions: alpha_CO = 4.0 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1; IR luminosity-to-SFR conversion factor = 1.73 x 10^-10 M_sun yr^-1 / L_sun (Salpeter 1-100 M_sun IMF)
